slot.brief: Given a small frequency/ungrouped data set, compute mean deviation about the mean (or median) step by step

stem: The table gives a data set with frequencies. Find its mean deviation about the median. $$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x_i&1&3&5&8\\f_i&2&3&2&2\end{array}$$
notes: from question bank gb815623dd07b (verified in job 20261127-132429-aa8a)
working:
$N=9,\quad m=3$\n$\text{MD}=\dfrac{2|1-3|+3|3-3|+2|5-3|+2|8-3|}{9}=\dfrac{18}{9}=2.$

Independent check: There are 9 observations, so the median is 3. The mean deviation is \(\frac{2|1-3|+3|3-3|+2|5-3|+2|8-3|}{9}=\frac{18}{9}=2\).
solution:
The total frequency is $N=9$, so the median is $m=3$. Hence,
$$\text{Mean deviation about median}=\frac{\sum f_i|x_i-m|}{N}=\frac{2|1-3|+3|3-3|+2|5-3|+2|8-3|}{9}=2.$$
